- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then drop sharply — suggesting lag in adjusting to downward momentum.
- After a spike in the history (e.g., 72+), model often overreacts with a high forecast, then undercorrects.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to recognize that prices often return to lower levels after peaks.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — model should dampen early peaks.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — especially in the 10–20 day range.
- Forecasting horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts are too bullish, especially when recent history shows volatility or downward trends.
